title: Probing the pairing symmetry of moiré graphene superconductors
authors: Sayak Biswas, Rajdeep Sensarma, Mohit Randeria
abstract: The pairing symmetry of magic-angle moiré graphene is a fundamental question that remains unresolved. Combining experimental and theoretical inputs, we constrain the superconducting order parameters that can emerge from the incommensurate Kekulé spiral (IKS) normal state on the hole-doped side of $ν= -2$. Imposing the additional experimental constraint of nodal superconductivity, we are left with the task of distinguishing between singlet or triplet pairing, and of determining the d-vector in the latter case. We propose definitive tests to identify the pairing symmetry based on two classes of experiments using the response of the superconducting state to Zeeman field orientation. The first set of predictions is for spectroscopic and thermodynamic measurements sensitive to low-energy excitations near the nodes. The second set is for phase-sensitive measurements of topologically protected Andreev bound states near boundaries, whose spectroscopy is shown to provide a smoking gun signature of the pairing symmetry.
summary: This work theoretically distinguishes between singlet and triplet superconducting pairing symmetries in moiré graphene by predicting distinct signatures. The authors leverage symmetry constraints and model both bulk quasiparticle excitations and interface-bound Andreev states. Observing the Zeeman field response of these two types of probes offers a definitive experimental pathway to characterize the underlying pairing mechanism.
main_problem: The primary goal is to definitively determine the pairing symmetry (singlet vs. triplet) of superconductivity in moiré graphene superconductors, and if triplet, to identify the direction of the d-vector.
main_result: Distinct signatures are predicted for singlet versus triplet pairing when probing the superconducting state using Zeeman fields applied either to bulk quasiparticles or at superconductor/insulator interfaces via Andreev bound states (ABS).
method: The analysis combines symmetry constraints ($\mathcal{T}, C_{2z}$) with theoretical modeling of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian, analyzing both low-energy Density of States (DOS) and phase-sensitive ABS spectroscopy.
model_or_system:
The system is magic-angle moiré graphene superconductors operating on the hole-doped side of $
u = -2$, characterized by a normal state constrained by an Incommensurate Kekulé Spiral (IKS).
key_observables: Low-energy Density of States $N(E)$ under Zeeman field, and the splitting/behavior of topologically protected Andreev Bound States (ABS) at interfaces.
important_parameters: Zeeman field orientation ($\vec{B}$ relative to $\hat{d}$), doping level, and proximity to nodal superconductivity.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes robustness in the low-energy limit, relies on symmetry constraints derived from the IKS normal state, and models ABS using a smooth interface approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Zeeman splitting of zero-field ABS peaks for singlet pairing (splitting to $\pm B$) versus the angle-dependent splitting observed for triplet pairing ($\vec{B} \parallel \hat{d}$ vs. $\vec{B} \perp \hat{d}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically constrains the order parameter using symmetry arguments, develops theoretical predictions for two key experimental probes (bulk DOS and interface ABS), and contrasts the expected signatures for singlet versus triplet pairing.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the use of topological protection in Andreev bound states and the detailed analysis of spin/momentum dependence under external fields provides rich theoretical tools applicable to understanding exotic quantum phases in engineered systems.
